ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), plus automated screening against consolidated United Nations Security Council (UNSC) sanctions lists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, Luxembourg national financial sanction lists (Mémorial B), and CSSF guidance on targeted financial sanctions. Continuous transaction monitoring must detect beneficial owners, directors, and direct/indirect controllers, with identification based on the 25% threshold or control via other means.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be entered on the RCS in French, German, or Luxembourgish; foreign scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must include 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' either before or after the identifying phrase, must not be contrary to public order, and must not be confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The proposed name is pre-cleared by the drafting notary through the RCS negative search. If the RCS rejects the name on grounds of identity, resemblance, or public policy, the applicant must file a reasoned administrative appeal with the RCS registrar within 15 days of notification. If the registrar upholds the rejection, appeal is lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'Arrondissement) under Article 27 of the Law of 10 August 1915; the court must be seized within one month of the registrar's final decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Administrative domiciliation via a licensed domiciliation agent is permitted only for a non-industrial commercial seat; the manufacturing of dental clear aligner sheets under ISIC 3250 and NAICS 339114 requires a physical production establishment, adequate equipment, qualified personnel, and substantive operations in Luxembourg. Therefore, a virtual office alone will not satisfy Luxembourg tax substance and commercial integrity requirements for this business scope.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 40% probability within the first three operating years of an unannounced on-site inspection by Luxembourg tax authorities, CSSF, labour inspectorate (ITM), or municipal officials, given the manufacturing and regulatory license components.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statu te_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 710-1 et seq. (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (Statuts) filed and published in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000; fully subscribed; cash shares paid up to at least 25% of nominal value at incorporation; funds deposited with a Luxembourg credit institution or held in escrow by the notary until the RCS filing certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the first board resolutions of the SARL are adopted as follows: (i) the share subscriptions set forth in the subscription schedule, representing the entire subscribed capital of EUR 12,000, are hereby confirmed and accepted; (ii) the registered office shall be established at [address] in Luxembourg, and the Articles of Association shall be so ratified; (iii) [Name] is appointed as manager (Gérant) with sole signature authority, and [Name] as statutory auditor if required; (iv) the manager is authorized to complete all formalities with the Luxembourg Business Registers, the notary, and the tax authorities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Corporate Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names via the RCS website or directly to the Commercial Register demonstrating nonexistence against the register. The chosen name must not be contrary to public order, must be distinguishable, and must include the legal form suffix 'SARL'. A name block is typically issued immediately or within one business day.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (lease or intent)
Notarized power of attorney if filed by a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name resembles an existing registration, file a written objection and submit a revised list of alternative names within five business days, or request a formal decision before the RCS registry judge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Notary ( Notaire) appointed by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft French-language Articles of Incorporation containing names, capital, registered office, share classes, management provisions, and purpose clause covering manufacture of medical devices, including dental clear aligner sheets. Appear before the notary with original ID documents, the capital amount evidenced as deposited, and the RCS name reservation certificate. The notary records the deed, verifies powers, and collects the subscription signatures.
required_dossiers: Proof of bank deposit of the paid-up capital or bank quarantine statement
ID documents of all shareholders and managers
Criminal record certificate for each manager (European format)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises drafting deficiencies, cure by amending the draft and re-submitting to the same notary. If any founder is unavailable, execute a notarized proxy or schedule a substitute notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) – Remote Electronic Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, file the notarial deed, the appointment of managers, and the registered office details with the RCS. Submit the electronic incorporation form with all required annexes, pay the registration fee, and receive the RCS registration number. The notary simultaneously submits the publication extract for RESA. The company acquires legal personality upon RCS registration; RESA publication follows automatically.
required_dossiers: List of managers and their signed acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query for missing documents, respond through the portal within one month. Failure to cure results in a refusal order; appeal before the Luxembourg district court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 40 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Security and General Taxation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS issuance, enroll for corporate income tax and municipal business tax, obtain a VAT identification number for manufacturing activities, register with CCSS for employer obligations, and apply for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) required for manufacturing operations. File all registrations electronically within 15 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Lease or property title for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT or CCSS reject a submission, rectify the form within 30 days. For VAT delays, use the Periodic VAT correction procedure or request a late registration waiver in writing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for Industry and Business Establishment (Direction Générale des PME et du Commerce)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued under the Law of 2 September 2011 on Business Establishment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class B – Mandatory registration and simplified environmental compliance statement for medical device thermoforming facilities; no full EIA report required below EU Annex thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: EU Urban Wastewater Directive 91/271/EEC and national discharge limits for COD ≤ 125 mg/L and total suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L; VOCs: emissions below EU Solvent Emissions Directive 1999/13/EC and Luxembourg VOC thresholds; plastic waste handling per Law on Waste Management and national recycling regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) confirming compliance with building fire extinguisher and escape route standards; structural load inspection certificate by a Luxembourg approved engineering office for all production machinery anchors and mezzanine loads; occupational workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering machine safety, personal protective equipment, and ergonomic requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; online portals: myGuichet.lu, eTVA, eCDF
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL must first be registered with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) to obtain a business registration number. Tax identification numbers are then automatically issued: a national tax number (NIF) from the ACD and a separate VAT identification number from the AEDT for taxable persons. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment must apply directly to the ACD (NIF) and the AEDT (VAT) using the VAT registration form (Formulaire 1), typically requiring a local approved tax representative for non-EU entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - SARL is a fully taxable resident company subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (communal trade tax), and the solidarity surcharge on worldwide income. Tax residence is based on place of effective management or statutory seat in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Luxembourg allows certain elections under specific regimes: VAT grouping (assujetti unique), fiscal unity for corporate income tax and municipal business tax (at least 95% ownership), and the 80% exemption for intellectual property income (IP box) are available. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD apply, and no elective avoidance of those rules is permitted.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA) - fully harmonised with EU VAT Directive (2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (annual taxable turnover for small business exemption, excluding certain cross-border supplies); no statutory threshold for mandatory registration of established businesses or non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time fiscal clearance and digital stamping are NOT required. E-invoicing is permitted subject to B2B customer consent. Mandatory e-invoicing in PEPPOL format for B2G supplies exceeding EUR 10,000 (for eligible public contracts). Periodic VAT returns (monthly/quarterly) and annual recapitulative statements (listings) of intra-Community supplies are filed via eTVA. SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) must be electronically submitted in XML format upon request by the tax authorities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) supply of goods dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or on behalf of the customer; (2) intra-Community supply of goods where the customer provides a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are transported to another Member State; (3) direct export of dental clear aligner sheets when the documentary evidence demonstrates physical departure from the EU within the prescribed time limits. Services physically performed on goods that are subsequently exported (e.g., processing) may be zero-rated under specific conditions.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are subject to strict documentary scrutiny by the Luxembourg VAT authorities. If documentation is insufficient or the export is not proven, VAT is retrospectively assessed at the standard rate, plus interest (default interest at 0.45% per month). Fraudulent claims (including false or forged export documentation) trigger penalties ranging from 10% to 200% of the evaded tax, monetary fines, criminal prosecution (imprisonment up to 5 years), and debarment from VAT valid registration. Directors may be held personally liable in cases of intentional misconduct.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); foreign exchange and capital movement policy is delegated to the Ministry of Finance (Trésor) and the European Central Bank within the Eurosystem; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent AML/CFT supervisor for credit institutions and payment service providers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union; Luxembourg applies no exchange controls, no surrender obligations, no prior authorization, and no quantitative limits for current account or capital account transactions. Profit remittances, shareholder loan repayments, royalties, and trade settlements are free, subject only to (i) domestic withholding tax rules on dividends (15% standard, fully reduced under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where a qualifying parent holds at least 10% of the capital for an uninterrupted 12-month period, or under Luxembourg tax treaties), (ii) EU/international sanctions and asset-freeze screening, and (iii) mandatory statistical reporting to the BCL for cross-border payments above EUR 12,500; no regulatory authorization is required for inbound equity transfer into a Luxembourg SARL, but the receiving bank must verify the capital increase notarial deed and the RCS update.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, endorsement, or retention rules for export proceeds; a Luxembourg SARL receiving dental aligner revenues in USD, CHF, or other currencies may retain the funds in a multicurrency account, convert at market rate, or hedge them freely. The only compulsory requirement is that every resident enterprise reports cross-border receipts to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistical purposes through its bank, applying the BPM6/ECB Regulation (EU) No 184/2005 coding grid; there is no minimum conversion ratio and no BCL purchase obligation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulation_reference: Law of 22 December 1998 on the BCL; ECB Regulation (EU) 184/2005 as amended; AML Law of 12 November 2004 as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02; Circular CSSF 21/788; Directive (EU) 2015/849.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.current_account_payments: Trade receivables, royalties, and service fees are paid free of control; remittance requires the bank to obtain the underlying commercial invoice, transport document, or contract, and the correct BOP purpose code; funds can be converted into EUR or USD spot without any limit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_account_payments: Inbound capital subscription, additional paid-in capital, shareholder advances, and outbound dividend distributions are unrestricted, but the corporate treasury must demonstrate that the SARL's net assets do not fall below the subscribed capital minimum of EUR 12,000 under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended; the bank will require an RCS excerpt reflecting the capital increase.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.sanctions_and_transfer_screening: All wire transfers are screened against EU, UN, and OFAC sanctions lists; transactions involving counterparties in sanctioned jurisdictions or with a residual compliance danger to the EU financial system may be blocked pending regulatory approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.profit_remittance_hurdle: No FX authorization hurdle, only tax clearance: a dividend distribution is generally payable 100% to the shareholder after the general meeting since the 15% withholding tax is collected by the paying bank via Form 3G in favor of the Administration des contributions directes; if the parent is EU/EEA resident and satisfies the participation threshold, a zero-rate withholding declaration must be filed ex ante. The bank will require the distribution minutes and a solvency certificate signed by the gérant, and the payment must be made via a Luxembourg credit institution to comply with beneficial owner disclosure.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account for the SARL share capital deposit and operational multicurrency current account (EUR, USD, CHF)
Operational corporate account with dedicated EUR/USD clearing and cross-border trade payment facility
Capital escrow account and daily treasury account; preferred for US-dollar inbound equity from a US parent
Operational account integrated with SG Luxembourg's cash pool and documentary credit desk
Specialized treasury account for large intra-group flows, FX hedging, and US-dollar clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a supplementary payments channel only, but legally insufficient as the sole treasury banking rail: a Luxembourg SARL may open a business account with a licenced e-money institution (e.g., a Luxembourg PFS or a passporting EU EMI under Directive 2009/110/EC) for pay-in/pay-out of volume card transactions and international supplier payments, provided that the EMI is authorized in the EEA and registered with the CSSF; however, an EMI cannot grant credit, cannot hold client deposits in the legal sense, and its safeguarding arrangement (segregated pool at a credit institution) creates third-party risk that fails the corporate treasury's liquidity-safety test. The finance ministry and BCL reporting obligations are not automatically discharged by the EMI; all cross-border reporting must be executed through the settlement bank, which makes the tier-1 credit institution account mandatory. For recurring B2C/Stripe card settlements, a payment institution acquiring partner is acceptable if settlement is directly into the SARL's BIL or BCEE account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, every Luxembourg tier-1 bank requires at least one physical appointment for the ultimate beneficial owner and the authorized signatory (gérant) at the bank's registered office or, exceptionally, at a Luxembourg notary or an EU embassy with notarial powers; there is no UBO-location exemption. Remote opening is procedurally possible only where the applicant is identified via a qualified electronic signature under eIDAS combined with a live video interview and the transmission of certified/copies of passports, notarized corporate documents, and apostilles; nevertheless, the AML Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02 still require the bank to identify the beneficial owner beyond reasonable doubt, and the onboarding committee of BCEE/BIL generally declines non-resident directors without an interview. Budget for a one-or-two-day Luxembourg visit by the UBO, the gérant, and the company secretary to sign the account agreement and execute the KYC declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office located in a shared mail-forwarding address with a mass file of shell companies; negative media alert from the press or previous suspicious activity report.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Current RCS excerpt (Extrait du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) not older than 30 days; (2) lease agreement for the Luxembourg business office with proof of physical utilization; (3) employer declaration and social security registration in Luxembourg; (4) audited accounts or opening balance sheet; (5) corporate governance chart identifying all directors; (6) business plan for thermoforming and automated trimming of dental aligners under ISIC 3250; (7) original electricity/telecom invoices; (8) professional indemnity notice.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a tax resident of a non-cooperative third jurisdiction or of a country on FATF high-risk/monitored list; or the UBO holds PEP status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg RBE register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) including a detailed ownership chain; (2) passport copy certifiée conforme with apostille and sworn translation; (3) source-of-wealth statement supported by tax assessments, bank references, and sale-and-purchase agreements; (4) PEP due-diligence questionnaire and declaration of expected account activity; (5) public sanctions-screening report (EU consolidated list, UN, OFAC) demonstrating no match.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction pattern inconsistent with a typical medical device trader: high-frequency small payments from Stripe/payment platforms, credit card acquirer volume, and intercompany loans with no clear commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Relevant product licence under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and the Law of 15 January 2021 on Medical Devices; (2) Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) registration certificate for the dental clear aligner sheets; (3) ISO 13485 certificate; (4) sample commercial invoices and delivery notes; (5) reconciliations of Stripe settlement to the production ERP; (6) information memorandum describing the dual-function of the SARL as aligner sheet manufacturer and intra-group distributor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore participation: foreign director or shareholder based in a jurisdiction where the bank cannot verify identity without in-person notarial evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Notarized special power of attorney for the gérant registered in Luxembourg; (2) apostilled company resolution authorizing the account opening; (3) legal opinion on the foreign entity's validity and solvency; (4) certified true copies of all passports plus an interview recording; (5) declaration on the source and purpose of the inbound equity contribution; (6) three years of audited financial statements of the direct parent if the parent corporate is non-EU.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.standard_onboarding_documentation: Business licence dossier comprising: notarized articles of incorporation and bylaws; RCS extract; RBE extract; VAT certificate; medical device registration; proof of health-insurance affiliation (CCM) for employees; register of directors; share register; resolution by the board; certified passport copies; UBO declaration; bank reference letters; cash-flow forecast for first 12 months; and proof of ownership of the address where the bank's acknowledgement letter must be sent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injection from the US/EU parent is executed through a standard SWIFT MT103 SEPA or MT202/202COV wire into the SARL's euro account at a Luxembourg tier-1 bank. The banking reference must contain the legal entity name (LU SARL), the notarial deed reference of the capital increase, and the BCL balance-of-payments purpose code 'S301' (Direct investment in a reporting enterprise - equity) or 'S331' for a shareholder loan, as applicable. The settlement bank will request, before crediting, an RCS excerpt showing the capital increase and the deposit certificate issued by the bank itself on day one; the account cannot be used for operational expenses until the notary certifies the capital subscription. For payment platforms (Stripe), the parent may also fund the SARL's Stripe balance via a linked payout bank account using MT103 with reference 'Stripe funding - aligned with BCL code S301/S331'; nevertheless, for FATF compliance, the accounting entry must match the purpose code and be supported by the equity transfer agreement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for thermoplastic pellets, PETG/TPU sheets, packaging materials, and laboratory consumables are routed via: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank supplier payments, with BOP purpose code 'S810' for goods imports and 'S891' for services, cross-referenced by the supplier's commercial invoice and bill of lading; (2) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 via SWIFT MT700 when the supplier requires an unconditional payment undertaking; (3) SWIFT MT760 standby LCs for security obligations; (4) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU suppliers; (5) SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) for urgent small disbursements, e.g., testing laboratory fees or customs duties; (6) card acquiring rails for B2C/B2B2C sales: Stripe settlement into the SARL's EUR settlement account via a Luxembourg or Belgian acquiring PSP. All outbound payments require online confirmation of the invoice, proof of goods receipt, and verification of the beneficiary against EU sanctions lists. For intra-group management fees and royalty payments to the parent, the SARL must maintain an intercompany services agreement and a transfer pricing file in accordance with Luxembourg arm's-length legislation (Article 56bis LIR).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD vanilla outright forwards (spot-deferred and fixed-date, up to 12 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Luxembourg-authorized credit institution or an EEA investment firm, subject to EMIR clearing and trade repository reporting obligations; designated as hedge accounting under IFRS 9 if the SARL qualifies.
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps (plain vanilla, fully collateralized under an ISDA CSA) to convert USD surplus from US-oriented dental aligner sales into EUR without transfer restrictions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD against non-convertible or restricted-delivery currencies of the target export markets (e.g., CNH, INR, BRL) where physical delivery is legally unavailable; NDFs are permitted only with an EU-authorized FX counterparty and fully documented against underlying trade or intercompany exposure; the notional must not exceed 110% of forecast aligned-practice cash flows in the relevant currency per the Luxembourg CSSF market-conduct expectations.

FX options (vanilla European call/put and zero-cost collars) for protecting payroll and dividend cash flows, allowed for hedging, not for speculative or leveraging treasury positions; regulated under the same EMIR/CSDR framework, requiring daily valuation and margining.

Foreign exchange spot contracts and banked automated dealing lines for monthly profit remittance and VAT payments; all hedging is executed within the documented treasury policy of the SARL, authorized by a board resolution, and reported to the BCL as part of the bank's balance-of-payments filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_clearing_principles: The SARL must maintain a full-service multi-currency relation with either BCEE or BIL for clearing; a purely Stripe-driven flow is operationally acceptable for B2C receipts but legally and prudentially insufficient for the treasury function. As a minimum liquidity standard, the company will hold its subscription capital and the equivalent of at least three months of operating costs in a demand deposit at the tier-1 bank; the maximum overnight balance at the EMI/payment partner is capped at EUR 20,000 to avoid issuer-custody risk, with daily sweep to the settlement account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.banking_fees_and_execution_timeline: Account opening for a straightforward SARL with one UBO and one authorized signatory costs between EUR 500 and EUR 2,500 per month including maintenance; the onboarding timeline is four to eight weeks from the notarial deed to full remote execution; a priority express KYC review can reduce the timeline to fifteen business days with a sponsoring reference from an existing bank client.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.prudential_and_regulatory_notes: All derivatives must be executed with a counterparty established in a Member State of the EU/EEA; the SARL is not a financial counterparty and is generally exempt from the EMIR mandatory clearing threshold if its aggregate gross notional of OTC derivatives stays below EUR 3,000 million, but it remains subject to the reporting obligation once the clearing threshold is exceeded; for a mid-size dental aligner manufacturer the threshold is not a practical concern; nonetheless, the treasury policy should cap the tenor at 12 months and never exceed the documented natural exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting – approval of statutory financial statements, allocation of result and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; internal act, no regulatory filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene exposes managers to civil liability; prevents lawful filing of annual accounts and may trigger regulatory enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved annual accounts with Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval and no later than seven months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers formal reminder, court-imposed order and monetary penalties; persistent non-filing may result in administrative strike-off from RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined direct tax return: corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax for the closed fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes – ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return for a financial year ending on 31 December is due by 31 December of the following calendar year; extensions available on formal request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to 10% of assessed tax; statutory late-payment interest accrues monthly; possible ex officio assessment and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (VAT form 3) for annual VAT position
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg VAT Administration (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return due by 1 May following the calendar year; quarterly or monthly returns follow assigned VAT filing periods
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to administrative fines and late-payment interest; repeat failures may expose responsible managers to penalty proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner (UBO/RBE) record and amendment filing where ownership changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual no-change confirmation due no later than 31 December of each calendar year; amendments due within one month of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or late UBO filings are punishable by administrative fines and criminal penalties against managers; RBE record may be exposed to AML enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL is exempt from mandatory audit if it does not exceed two of the three Luxembourg thresholds: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount 50 employees. Exceeding the thresholds, or being a public-interest entity or a group subsidiary subject to parent group audit instructions, requires an independent certified audit by an approved réviseur d'entreprises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory accounts are prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (Code de commerce and CSSF chart of accounts); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for individual accounts and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed parents.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Before each annual general meeting, management must reconcile the RBE record against the register of members. Any transfer of SARL interests must be evidenced in writing and entered in the register of members; the RBE must be updated within one month of the transfer. If no change occurred, the existing RBE registration is confirmed annually on the LBR portal before the 31 December deadline.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members (registre des parts sociales / actionnaires)
Register of directors' resolutions and board meeting minutes
Minute book of shareholders' meetings (procès-verbaux d'assemblées générales)
Register of beneficial owners extract (RBE file)
Accounting books, ledgers and supporting vouchers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 – 2,400 per year (approx. EUR 1,000 – 2,200) for registered office and professional corporate secretarial/registered agent service in Luxembourg City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – 15,000 per year for certified audit of a small- to mid-sized manufacturing SARL; accounting and compliance support quoted separately

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined rate: 17% corporate income tax on taxable profits above EUR 175,000; 7% solidarity surcharge; 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% corporate income tax band on the first EUR 175,000 of taxable profit (combined 22.80% in Luxembourg City); 80% IP Box exemption for qualifying intangible income (effective rate approximating 4.99% on IP-derived profits); 50% R&D super-deduction and refundable R&D tax credit of up to 30% of eligible R&D expenditures (capped at EUR 300,000 per tax year); municipal business tax is deductible in computing the corporate income tax base; participation exemption fully exempting qualifying dividends and capital gains from EU and treaty-resident subsidiaries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 750 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed with the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via the MyGuichet.lu electronic filing portal (eCDF/eLIR) using a Luxtrust or EU eID electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 December of the calendar year following the tax year (e.g., 31 December 2025 for the tax year ending 31 December 2024); extensions may be granted upon reasoned application to the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RCSL registration number, Luxembourg tax identification number (NIN), legal name, legal form (SARL), and registered office address in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) files Form 750 using the PE's Luxembourg address and the foreign corporate identification data; a company without a Luxembourg PE is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax and must not file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Category of collective entity and confirmation of taxable residence; resident SARLs are subject to unlimited tax liability on worldwide income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers select the limited tax liability category; the foreign tax residence certificate must be attached where treaty relief is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The accounting profit or loss before tax per the statutory annual accounts approved by the shareholders' meeting; financial statements must be filed with the RCSL within one month of approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE: report the PE's separate profit and loss statement prepared under Luxembourg GAAP or a reconcilable standard (IAS/IFRS with adjustments).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items: 50% of entertainment and representation expenses, non-deductible gifts, fines and penalties, taxes charged on the tax base itself, and any interest, royalties, or fees exceeding arm's length amounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same add-backs apply to the Luxembourg PE; recharge of head-office costs is deductible only when supported by arm's length allocation records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income: qualifying dividends and capital gains under the participation exemption; 80% of qualifying net IP Box income; and municipal business tax actually incurred.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are available to the PE only where the PE holds the participation or exploits the qualifying intellectual property through its Luxembourg operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unrelieved tax losses brought forward under the 17-year rule; the set-off is denied where the company has ceased its actual activity and the operation is deemed artificial or the shareholding continuity test is abused.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses suffered by a foreign head office cannot be set off against Luxembourg PE profits; only PE-specific losses are available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 15%/17% progressive IRC scale; solidarity surcharge at 7% of IRC; municipal business tax at the communal rate (Luxembourg City: 6.75%); final computation of the total effective charge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE is taxable only on Luxembourg-source business income; no net wealth tax assessment arises where the PE's attributed capital is below the applicable exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed schedule of cross-border transactions with affiliated enterprises: category, counterparty, amount, pricing policy, and transfer pricing method applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for non-resident PEs carrying out related-party transactions through the Luxembourg branch; failure to attach the schedule triggers a specific non-disclosure penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of up to EUR 250 per return; formal notice followed by a surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax; late payment: default interest of 0.6% per commenced month (7.2% per annum) plus enforcement costs; fraudulent non-filing is prosecuted as tax fraud with fines up to EUR 66,500 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The dividend payer may apply the domestic exemption or treaty reduction only upon submission of a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the shareholder's tax authority, a beneficial-ownership declaration, and proof of the shareholding percentage and holding period. For the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (Directive 2011/96/EU) 0% rate, the Luxembourg parent or EU parent must hold at least 10% of the share capital or have an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million and satisfy the 12-month minimum holding period and the anti-abuse substance test; an advance exoneration request (Formulaire 702) is filed with the ACD before the distribution. If relief is not granted at source, the withholding agent deducts the 15% statutory tax and the beneficial owner claims a refund from the ACD within the ordinary limitation period (generally five years), attaching the TRC, the withholding certificate, and proof of actual receipt.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on ordinary arm's length interest or royalty payments made to non-resident beneficiaries; the statutory 15% dividend withholding tax may nevertheless apply where excessive interest or royalties are recharacterized as hidden profit distributions (profit-participating loans, non-arm's length pricing). No treaty reduction is required for royalties or interest because the domestic rate is already 0%; however, the recipient remains taxable in its state of residence, and the payer must evidence the arm's length nature and the beneficial ownership of the income to avoid reclassification.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 1,000,000 — aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions above this threshold trigger the mandatory Local File obligation; a Master File is required when the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000; Country-by-Country reporting applies to groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000 under EU DAC4. Below the threshold, a simplified Annex 6 declaration is filed with Form 750.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply sectoral Economic Substance Regulations in the UAE/Barbados style; nevertheless, Article 6 of the Luxembourg Tax Adaptation Law (ATAD GAAR), the judicial doctrine of fraus legis, and the Principal Purpose Test under the Multilateral Instrument (MLI Article 29(9)) require genuine economic substance. A dental clear aligner manufacturing SARL must maintain real production facilities, qualified operational and quality-control staff, active local management decisions, physical bank accounts, and substance proportionate to its contractual functions (manufacturing, sourcing, IP exploitation, and financing). Without such substance, the ACD may deny treaty benefits, the 80% IP Box exemption, loss carryforwards, or recharacterize intra-group payments as constructive dividends.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of manufacturing or e-commerce revenue, fabrication of supplier invoices for thermoformed aligner materials, concealment of intra-group management fees, or destruction of accounting records before the mandatory 10-year retention period expires.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under the Luxembourg General Tax Act: fine up to EUR 66,500 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years; civil recovery of evaded tax with monthly default interest of 0.6% and a surcharge of up to 10%; the company's tax clearance certificate may be revoked, rendering it ineligible for public tenders and regulated licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fraudulent returns or divert corporate assets to evade tax incur joint and several civil liability for the company's tax shortfall under the Luxembourg Companies Law (action en responsabilité), personal criminal fines and imprisonment, travel bans and asset freezes imposed by the investigating judge, and disqualification from managing Luxembourg entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL without genuine production staff, with foreign management directing the aligner operations, using mailbox premises solely to access treaty benefits or the IP Box regime, and lacking board minutes or operational substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disapplication of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test and the GAAR; full taxation of the diverted income; reversal of the 80% IP Box exemption; denial of loss carryforwards; administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 under DAC6 abusive arrangement disclosure rules; possible strike-off from the Luxembourg trade register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and executive directors who knowingly enable the artificial interposition are liable jointly and severally for the restored taxes and interest; they face criminal prosecution for aiding tax fraud, suspension of management functions, travel bans during investigation, and personal guarantee of tax debts where assets have been stripped from the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and hidden profit distribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling dental aligner sheets to a related foreign distributor below arm's length price, paying inflated royalties for head-office IP to a zero-tax affiliate, or charging excessive shareholder interest without a TNMM benchmark study.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward transfer pricing adjustment under Article 56a LIR; recharacterization of the excess as constructive dividend subject to 15% withholding tax; default interest of 0.6% per month; additional assessment surcharge of up to 10%; if documentation is not produced, the ACD may use estimated assessments and shift the burden of proof; separate fine of up to EUR 250 for missing annexes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally set non-arm's length terms to strip the Luxembourg manufacturing margin breach their fiduciary duty and may be held personally liable for the resulting tax shortfall; aggravated conduct triggers criminal tax evasion charges, travel bans, and court-ordered capital reinstatement from the directors' personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving Stripe and platform credit card settlements into undisclosed foreign accounts, processing payments for sanctioned or fictitious dental distributors, failing to maintain the register of beneficial owners (RBE), or structuring transactions to avoid anti-money laundering screening.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg Criminal Code money laundering offences: imprisonment from 1 to 10 years and fines from EUR 12,500 up to EUR 1,250,000 depending on habitualness; RBE register violations carry fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and the court may suspend distributions; payment processors may terminate the SARL's merchant agreement and the entity may be barred from holding regulated authorizations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly process or conceal illicit proceeds face personal criminal liability with custodial sentences, travel bans and asset freezes by the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor, civil liability for compensation to affected third parties, and disqualification from serving as directors of any Luxembourg company for up to 10 years.
